svg.text: Test B grounding: one ground return per cable, tied locally in three groups
Grey tube = coax shield (ground). Inside it, the signal wire. At the far end each BNC-to-grabber cable splits into a red (signal) and a black (shield) grabber.
every SMA's outer shell is soldered to it
AGND–CGND/VEE joined by the TP15–TP13 link (keep)
On board ground pins: only COM and the TP link.
Group 2 (IN+): both black grabbers + CH1 ground together.
CH1 tip on the J1 cable's red grabber (board side of the 100 Ω).
As built, the 100 Ω is at the FAR end of the J1 cable, so the
cable (~100 pF/m) hangs directly on IN+. Note it in results.
Group 1 (IN−): both black grabbers + capacitor ground
As built, the 100 nF is at the FAR end of the J3 cable. A cable
shorted at one end can ring (quarter-wave stub; ~27 MHz for ~1.9 m).
The capacitor in J4 holds IN− at the board instead.
Group 3 (outputs): J7 + J8 black grabbers joined;
CH3 and CH4 grounds on that link.
100 Ω at the FAR end is correct here: it stands
in for the receiver at the end of the line.
If J7 has a plain BNC cable: its shell, via a
BNC-to-grabber adapter, to the same link.
Why a black grabber already IS board ground
→ SMA connector's outer shell (soldered to it)
→ black grabber at the far end
Metal touching metal the whole way: no extra wire needed. DMM check ≈ 0 Ω.
Don't: clip any black grabber or probe ground to a board pin too (a second path = a loop).
Don't: add wires between the three groups (they already meet through the board).
Revised 23 Nov 2026: CH1 added; part positions as built; J4 capacitor recommended
